# Complexity Insights

> Complexity Insights is an independent economics research house founded by Nicholas Thomas, based in Washington, D.C. It combines traditional econometrics with complexity science — agent-based modeling, network science, and non-linear dynamics — applied to financial and economic systems.

The research covers market simulation, supply-chain and exposure networks, systemic and tail-risk indicators, and M&A/integration analysis. It publishes applied research and essays.

## Pages

- [Home](https://complexityinsights.com/): Thesis, research areas, and current work
- [Projects](https://complexityinsights.com/projects/): Research projects in progress and published
- [Writings](https://complexityinsights.com/writings/): Working papers and essays on traditional and complexity economics
- [About](https://complexityinsights.com/about/): The research house and its founder, Nicholas Thomas

## Current work

- [United-Continental Merger Analysis](https://complexityinsights.com/writings/did-the-united-continental-merger/): Difference-in-differences analysis of 13.7 million observations, estimating the effect of the United-Continental airline merger on consumers. Weighs firm and consumer welfare and concludes the merger does not appear to have harmed consumers once recession recovery and fuel effects are accounted for.
- Designing a Better Job Market: A two-part study of why entry-level hiring clears so poorly. Part I diagnoses the market; Part II simulates a deferred-acceptance clearinghouse against today's open-application process.
- Data Ingestion Project: A multi-layer scraping, cleaning, and standardization pipeline that produces model-ready data for agent-based models.

## Founder

Nicholas Thomas — economist (B.S. Economics, Penn State University, 2025), Washington, DC metro area. Core stack: Python · R · Stata · Julia · SQL · NetworkX. Open to full-time roles in economic research, data analysis, and financial modeling.
